authority_boundary: Harness discovery produces candidate opportunities. It does not install harnesses, copy private code, claim state-of-the-art status, or authorize repo mutation.

radar_inputs.reason: Cold assets and missing-part links can reveal repeatable coding harness opportunities.
Repeated candidate tactics should graduate into harnesses when they need scripts, evals, or prompts.
Repos using or watching DAD assets can report friction that deserves a reusable harness.
External research may seed better harnesses, but output remains candidate-only until reviewed.

opportunity_signals.reason: Slow or broad Python test batteries deserve orchestration, selection, timing, and risk-gate harnesses.
Rust acceleration needs same-scope parity, mismatch audit, and timing claim gates.
Agent coding quality improves when instructions are evaluated as reusable, versioned assets.
Private-to-public movement needs provenance, release, and sensitive-content checks.
Cross-repo rollout needs harnesses that prevent accidental mutation and repo spam.
DAD needs repeatable methods for recognizing useful assets and preserving source pointers.

candidate_harness_families.goal: Find high-value reusable digital assets from repo scans without copying sensitive content.
Evaluate whether coding agents obey DAD style, preflight, harness, and non-negotiable instructions.
Turn orphan radar and external research into reviewed coding-improvement harness candidates.

external_research_policy.rule: External research may be summarized with links and provenance, but it must not be promoted, installed, or shared to public-facing repos without license, security, compatibility, and source-visibility review.

promotion_gates: README explains when to use and when not to use
source evidence and public/private safety are recorded
human or senior-agent review approves promotion from candidate
